notes: Both stable isotopes have I = 3/2. Ground-state A is derived from the directly measured hyperfine splitting (Delta nu = 2A). The 3d9 4s4p 4P3/2 level (40114.01 cm^-1) is included because the 249.2 nm line carries the only isotope shift that could be sourced. A_s / rme_J_ea0 for the two resonance lines are derived from the Carlsson et al. 1989 lifetimes after subtracting the weak 2P-2D branches with NIST A values (notes say 'derived'); all other A_s entries are CIPT theory from Dzuba et al. 2021 for the E2/M1 lines NIST does not list; no theory is entered for the 2P-2D E1 lines because NIST has measured A values. rme convention: A = 2.02613e18 |d|^2 / (lambda_vac[Angstrom]^3 (2J'+1)), J' the upper level. The two copper-vapour-laser lines are 3d10 4p 2P3/2 -> 3d9 4s2 2D5/2 (510.6 nm) and 2P1/2 -> 2D3/2 (578.2 nm); the E2 clock lines are 2S1/2-2D5/2 at 892.6 nm and 2S1/2-2D3/2 at 755.0 nm. Extra keys beyond the schema: ionization_energy, g_J_ratio_to_Cs133, hyperfine_anomaly_percent, E2_amplitude_au, lifetime_alternatives. Second pass: hyperfine constants marked "Kurucz" are read from R. L. Kurucz's Cu I hyperfine input files (uncertainty-free, second-hand; entries whose reference code there is LLLcalc are calculations and carry method "theory"). Isotope shifts of the 510.6, 515.3 and 521.8 nm lines are second-hand from Popov et al. (arXiv:1907.02920) with the sign converted to nu(63) - nu(65). Added levels not drawn on the site: 4P5/2, 4F9/2 (metastable, atomic-beam hyperfine data), 5s 2S1/2, 6p-9p 2P (lifetimes).
